isolation_policy: bubblewrap mount namespace: only the workspace, the policy-accepted read allowlist and the opencode runtime exist; the repository, the other arms' results, the earlier sessions and the global opencode configuration (its MCP servers and plugins) are not mounted; plus the opencode v2 permission object (bash denied, edit and write denied, read and external_directory deny-by-default with the explicit allowlist)
limitations: The mount namespace is the filesystem guarantee; the model provider is reachable over the shared network, so a model that was shown a file can still send it away.
sandbox_argv:
This exploration produces ONE mechanism. You are one of three independent reviewers; you see the same frozen evidence bundle and the same proposals as the others, and you do not coordinate with them before handing in.
THE RESEARCH OBJECTIVE:
Discover new mechanisms in which TRAINING-ONLY user behaviour and HYPERBOLIC geometry are computationally coupled to improve the RQ-VAE Semantic IDs used by a generative next-item recommender, with the real target of Stage3 test Recall@10 above 0.065.
THE SCOPE CONTRACT (a proposal that misses it is sent back, not scored):
A proposal is IN SCOPE only when all of this holds:
  1. BEHAVIOUR: it names one training-only behaviour signal (directed item transitions, user-interest branching, sequential co-consumption, popularity-adjusted graph neighbours, behaviour-conditioned assignment weights, ...) and says how it is computed.
  2. HYPERBOLIC GEOMETRY: it names an explicit curved operation (trainable or fixed negative curvature, Poincare or Lorentz distance, exp/log maps, geodesic scoring, curved residual, curved quantization, curved regularization) and where in training or quantization it acts.
  3. REAL COUPLING: one connected computational pathway uses both, so that removing either changes the core computation. A behaviour suffix on an unchanged Euclidean quantizer, a standalone hyperbolic loss beside an unrelated behaviour loss, a geometry name without geometric computation, or inherited unused hyperbolic code do NOT qualify.
  4. TESTABLE EFFECT: it states what should observably change (SID assignment, gradient or parameter update, prefix behaviour predictability, or Stage3 Recall) and names the behaviour-off, geometry-off/Euclidean and both-on comparisons. The three switches must be part of the mechanism, so that the coupling can be shown to be real, but the round RUNS no ablation arm: each candidate is trained once.
  5. MINIMAL SPECIFICATION: equations or pseudocode, inputs and outputs, numerical safeguards and the training cost. No proof and no paper section are required.
SID quality (ER, prefix counts, collisions) is NOT a scope criterion and NOT an admission rule.

EXPERIMENT POLICY (binding on every proposal, implementation and review):
  - ONE candidate, ONE training run, on the frozen budget (3000 Stage 2 epochs on four cards, the frozen Stage 3 protocol, no early stopping).
  - NO ablation experiments: the behaviour-off, geometry-off and both-on switches must EXIST in the code and must be correct, but no arm is trained with them switched off.
  - NO tuning experiments: no sweep over the coupling weight, the clip bound, the temperature, the usage weight or any other constant. A constant that enters the mechanism has to be DERIVED (a scale-relative bound, a measured quantity, a documented default), not chosen by trying values.
  - NO multi-seed experiments: a candidate is not repeated with other seeds, so a single run decides it and the seed noise is part of the uncertainty.
  - The behavioural diagnostics (coherence, adjacency, transfer predictability) are recorded, never used as an admission gate; Stage 3 test_recall@10 is the judgement.
  - A proposal that needs an ablation, a sweep or a seed repetition to make its case is out of programme: it has to make the case with one run.
THE SELECTION POLICY (rank-2026-10-v1): the reviewers RANK the proposals. The proposal the reviewers place best, in total, is the round's mechanism. Rank every proposal, best first, and give each one a reason that names the evidence you used.
Read the frozen evidence bundle for each proposal before you place it: a placement you cannot ground in the evidence is not a placement.
Write PLAIN TEXT, one line per proposal, in exactly this shape:
RANK: <idea_id> | position=<1 for the best, then 2, 3, ...> | reason=<one line>
RANK: <idea_id> | position=<n> | reason=<one line>
Every proposal must appear exactly once, the positions must be 1..N with no ties and no gaps, and the reason must say what in the evidence put the proposal there. If you cannot ground a proposal in the evidence, rank it last and say so in its reason; do not leave a proposal out.
THE PROPOSALS:
IDEA: nullcurv-hinge-rq
TITLE: A size-preserving null-calibrated curvature hinge on the per-level code quotient learns the per-level curvature of a hyperbolic RQ-VAE quantizer
MOTIVATION: The curvature forensics over 182 SID tables say the informative object is not a level's raw quotient-graph curvature (Spearman +0.03, p=0.65, confounded by level size) but the size-preserving-null-standardised curvature profile and specifically its across-level slope: standardised level-3 curvature correlates +0.26 with recall (+0.34 on mechanism families, p=0.001), level-1 curvature correlates -0.16, and their difference is -0.20 (p=0.0095), so SIDs whose prefix quotient curvature rises with depth recall better. Today that number is only a post-hoc predictor of finished SIDs. This idea turns the slope into a training-time design target: the RQ-VAE must produce a code partition whose standardised quotient curvature is non-decreasing in depth, and the only free variables that can satisfy that target are the per-level curvature values of the hyperbolic metric the quantizer assigns in. Level 1 is therefore pushed toward the expander-like end and level 3 toward the clustered end, which is the direction the data wants and is the opposite of the Issue #127 failure, where the coarse level was aligned to a 17-cell behavioural partition, collapsed to 4 codes and fell to 0.0513.
NOVELTY: Three things are new relative to everything already tried here. (1) The curvature parameter of the space is not set by a formula from a behavioural score (the CURVCTRL-SID shape), not a per-item rank or radius (the BRad-RQ shape) and not a successor-weighted Frechet mean (the round-128 shape): each level's curvature is a trainable parameter whose gradient is supplied by a hinge on the standardised curvature of the partition the quantizer is actually producing, so curvature becomes an output of a matching problem, not an input knob. (2) The matching target is the null-standardised, group-size-controlled quantity, so the level-size confound that made the raw curvature useless is removed inside the loop; the null (10 membership shuffles with the code histogram held fixed) is re-estimated every 250 epochs from the current partition. (3) The target is a profile order (level 1 <= level 2 <= level 3), not a level-wise absolute value, so no level is pinned to a number and no constant has to be chosen; the hinge margin is 0, which is the sign boundary of the measured -0.20 effect, not a tuned value.
CHANGE: Replace the Euclidean nearest-code metric of the frozen RQ-VAE with a per-level Lorentz distance of trainable curvature c_l, and add one loss term that penalises any inversion of the standardised Ollivier-curvature profile of the soft code quotient; the gradient of that term flows into c_l only, and c_l is the same quantity that selects codes, so the partition and the metric are optimised against each other through a single path.
SPECIFICATION: {'text': 'Frozen protocol objects unchanged: encoder f_phi, L = 3 residual levels, codebook size K per level (K = 256 used for all arithmetic below), Euclidean reconstruction, straight-through assignment, 3000 Stage-2 epochs, 24 steps/epoch, batch floor(24556/24) = 1023 items. Behaviour graph from the training split only: W[i,j] = n(i->j) + n(j->i) over consecutive pairs of training sequences, degree-normalised W~[i,j] = W[i,j]/sqrt(d_i d_j), d_i = sum_j W[i,j], sparsified to the 20 largest entries per row. Per-level curvature eta_l in R trainable with eta_l(0) = 0, c_l = c_0 exp(eta_l), documented default c_0 = 1.0, eta_l clipped to [-2.3, +2.3]. Tangent codebook a_{l,k} in R^d, atom e_{l,k} = exp_0^{c_l}(a_{l,k}); encoder residual u_i^(l) = z_i - sum_{m<l} log_0^{c_m}(e_{m,k_m}); the point quantised is v_i^(l) = u_i^(l)/(1 + ||u_i^(l)||/r_max) with numeric guard r_max = 10. Selection k_l = argmin_k d_{L,c_l}(v_i^(l), e_{l,k}); the frozen Euclidean commitment is replaced one-for-one by d^2_{L,c_l}(v_i^(l), e_{l,k}) with no new coefficient; the decoder keeps consuming the tangent vectors sum_l a_{l,k_l}, so the generative Stage-3 interface is untouched. Behaviour-curvature target inside the step: p_l(i,k) = softmax_k(-d_{L,c_l}(v_i^(l), e_{l,k})/tau_l), tau_l = 1/sqrt(c_l); B_l = P_l^T W~_batch P_l symmetrised; lazy walk m_a = 0.5 e_a + 0.5 B_l[a,:]/sum(B_l[a,:]); kappa_l(a,b) = 1 - W1(m_a, m_b)/d_{L,c_l}(e_{l,a}, e_{l,b}) with W1 an entropic Sinkhorn (3 iterations, eps = 0.05 * mean_{a,b} d_{L,c_l}, a measured scale) on the 8x8 support; kappa-hat_l = mass-weighted mean over the top-128 edges of B_l by mass; standardise kappa-tilde_l = (kappa-hat_l - mu_l)/max(sigma_l, 0.05|mu_l| + 1e-6) where mu_l, sigma_l come from R = 10 shuffles of the item->code map preserving the code histogram, recomputed every 250 epochs from the current hard partition; L_curv = max(0, kappa-tilde_1 - kappa-tilde_2)^2 + max(0, kappa-tilde_2 - kappa-tilde_3)^2; L = L_RQ + lambda * L_curv with lambda = L_RQ(step 0)/max(L_curv(step 0), 1e-6) measured once at initialisation.'}
COST: Per step at the frozen scale (24556 items, 1023 per step, 24 steps/epoch, 3000 epochs = 72,000 steps): three K x K Lorentz distance matrices (3 x 65,536 pairs x d = 32, about 6.3M MAC), three P^T W~ P products (3 x 256 x 1023 x 256, about 200M MAC, i.e. 0.4 GFLOP, three small GEMMs), three Sinkhorn blocks of 128 edges x 8 x 8 x 3 iterations (about 74k flops), plus a 1023 x 256 softmax x 3 per level. Total about 0.4 GFLOP per step, roughly 1-3 ms on one modern GPU, i.e. +2 to +5 percent over the baseline step; over 72,000 steps about +2 to +4 minutes of wall clock. The null re-estimation runs 12 times at 12 x 10 shuffles x 3 levels x 0.4 GFLOP, about 25 GFLOP total, under a minute. Extra memory: 3 x 256 x 256 floats for the quotient and 3 x 256 x 256 for the code distance matrix, under 2 MB. No extra forward or backward pass through the encoder or decoder.
HYPOTHESIS: Worth keeping only if all three hold in the single run: (a) the learned curvatures move off their default, |eta_l| >= 0.05 for at least one level by epoch 3000, which proves the behaviour term reached the geometry rather than being absorbed elsewhere; (b) the produced SID's standardised profile becomes non-decreasing in the hard partition too (both hinge terms below 0.05 by the final null re-estimate) while the level-3 used-code count stays at or above 0.9x its epoch-0 count, which shows the target was met without the Issue #127 collapse; (c) Stage-3 test_recall@10 exceeds 0.065.
RISKS: ['(1) The differentiable curvature surrogate may be dominated by the temperature and the sampled edge set rather than by the partition, so eta_l drifts for reasons unrelated to behaviour and (a) passes while (c) fails. (2) The target is measured on the level-l code-marginal quotient (K nodes) rather than on the level-l prefix-tuple quotient used in the forensics (up to K^l nodes), because a per-step null over prefix tuples is outside the step budget; the marginal may have the opposite slope for some tables. (3) Hyperbolic arccosh gradients blow up when two codes coincide, which is exactly the collapse mode of #127; the radial squash, the tau floor and the usage guard are the only defences and they may not be enough. (4) At level 3 the partition is nearly pure, so the shuffle null can have a near-zero sigma and kappa-tilde explodes and hijacks the total loss; the sigma floor mitigates but also weakens the signal. (5) With one run and no ablation, a null result cannot distinguish "the slope target is wrong" from "the surrogate gradient is bad", and that ambiguity must be reported rather than resolved.']
END IDEA

IDEA: CURVALLOC-LORENTZ-RQ
TITLE: Mean-zero allocation of per-level Lorentz curvature and code radius from the null-standardised Ollivier curvature of the training behaviour quotient graph
MOTIVATION: The measured evidence says the recall-relevant geometric object is the level-wise profile of the behaviour quotient graph's standardised Ollivier curvature (L3 +0.26, L1 -0.16, L1-L3 -0.20, p=0.0095), and that the largest non-geometric driver is how many level-3 codes actually get used (+0.42, collisions -0.39). Existing SIDs differ only in whether their prefix geometry happens to fit the level-wise clustering of the behaviour graph. No quantizer currently builds that fit: the partition comes from one Euclidean nearest-code rule with a single curvature shared by all three levels.
NOVELTY: Not a per-level learning rate from a hard prefix-transition score (CURVCTRL-SID), not entropy-ranked radial assignment (BRad-RQ), not Frechet codebook updates, and not a fixed mixed-curvature product chosen by hand. The signal is a runtime-measured, permutation-null-standardised Ollivier curvature of the behaviour quotient graph induced by the CURRENT prefix assignment, spent as a mean-zero allocation of two geometric quantities (per-level negative curvature c_l and per-level radial budget rho_l) that enter the distance the quantizer itself minimises. No extra loss term is added, no recall label is used, and the assignment feeds back into the measurement, so behaviour and geometry form a closed loop rather than two parallel objectives.
CHANGE: Each RQ level l lives on its own Lorentz hyperboloid of curvature -c_l with code radius rho_l, both set from that level's standardised behaviour-quotient curvature, c_l = c0*exp(-delta_l) and rho_l = rho0*exp(delta_l/2) with delta_l = kappa_hat_l - mean_l(kappa_hat_l). Nearest-code assignment, residual subtraction and codebook parameterisation all pass through the exp/log maps of that level's hyperboloid, so changing delta_l changes which code each item receives.
SPECIFICATION: {'text': "(1) Build W once from the training split: W_ij = number of training sessions in which j occurs after i within the same window H used by the sequential Stage-2 encoder, symmetrised W <- (W+W^T)/2; N_tr = 24556. (2) Every T = 200 epochs (15 refreshes over 3000 epochs) take the current hard prefixes p_l(i) = (k_1..k_l) and form the quotient graph Q_l: nodes = occupied level-l prefixes, A_l(a,b) = sum_{i in a, j in b} W_ij (sparse S_l^T W S_l, self-loops kept); d_Q = unweighted hop distance. (3) Lazy walk P = 0.5(I + D^{-1}A) with D = diag(A1); curvature kappa(a,b) = 1 - W1(m_a, m_b)/d_Q(a,b) with m_a = 0.5*delta_a + 0.5*A_a./deg(a). (4) Standardise against a member-shuffling null: R = 8 relabellings of items into prefixes with group sizes preserved, kappa_hat_l = (kappa_bar_l - mu_null,l)/sigma_null,l, the same edge sample size used in both. (5) Form delta_l with the mean-zero constraint, clip to [-1,+1], EMA with 0.5. (6) All distances, residuals and codebooks use the level's own hyperboloid. STOP-GRADIENT on kappa_hat: it is a schedule, not a loss."}
COST: Per step the extra work is three Lorentz distance tensors of shape B x K x (D+1) plus three exp/log maps of shape B x D per item and per code: about 1.2e6 extra flops at B=256, K=256, D=64, under 2% of a step, with no backward pass through the measurement. The 15 curvature refreshes cost one sparse S_l^T W S_l per level (3 x nnz(W) ~ 3e6 adds), 8 null relabellings, and 3 levels x 256 sampled edges x 30 Sinkhorn iterations on supports of at most 9+9 cells (~1.5e7 flops per refresh, a few seconds each), so roughly 30-60 s of the whole 72000-step run: under 1% wall clock and no extra memory beyond one 24556 x 3 assignment cache.
HYPOTHESIS: If level-wise clustering of the training behaviour graph is a real constraint on a good prefix code, then letting the more clustered sub-quotient (typically level 3) own a flatter, wider hyperboloid while the more branching level (typically level 1) owns a sharper, tighter one must (a) keep level-3 code usage at or above baseline, (b) not collapse level-1 usage, (c) make the run's measured standardised profile monotone in depth, and (d) push Stage3 test Recall@10 above 0.065. Observed from the run's own logs: per-level used-code counts, the 15 recorded kappa_hat triples, and test_recall@10 against 0.065; if the profile is not monotone or level-1 usage falls below about 8 codes the hypothesis is falsified.
RISKS: ['The sign of the curvature-to-geometry map may be wrong for this data (flatter may need to follow LOW curvature), and one run cannot correct it; the +-1 clip keeps the worst case a bounded factor-e perturbation of one level instead of a collapse. The assignment<->curvature loop can oscillate, damped by the T=200 cadence, EMA 0.5 and the mean-zero constraint. Sinkhorn W1 on sparse quotient graphs is noisy and biased upward; the identical estimator is applied to the null so standardisation cancels the bias but amplifies variance when sigma_null is small, hence the sigma floor. The tangent-space residual chain is less faithful than the Euclidean one and can degrade reconstruction; the measured radial normalisation makes the tanh squash near-identity for typical items.']
END IDEA

IDEA: ORC-CELLCHART
TITLE: Behaviour-curvature cell charts: per-code standardised Ollivier curvature sets each RQ codeword's own Poincare chart curvature used in assignment
MOTIVATION: The SID's prefix geometry is fixed and Euclidean for every codeword, so a codeword sitting on a tree-like (branching) behavioural neighbourhood and one sitting inside a cohesive cluster are forced to discriminate residuals identically. The forensics show the standardised level profile, not the raw curvature, is what tracks recall, and that level-3 code usage and collisions dominate. What is missing is a mechanism that gives each codeword a geometry matched to its own behavioural quotient neighbourhood, at the level's own resolution, without ever coarsening the partition.
NOVELTY: Earlier rounds set a per-LEVEL curvature from a scalar (hard prefix-transition score) or a per-code radius from context entropy. This sets a per-CODE curvature MAGNITUDE from the standardised Ollivier-Ricci curvature of that code's node in the level's behaviour quotient, expressed as a deviation from a resolution-matched behaviour reference partition (exactly K_l cells), and makes that number the curvature of that code's Poincare chart inside the nearest-code rule. The curvature is not a loss, a schedule or a radius: it is the metric in which the residual-to-codeword distance is measured, per code, per level.
CHANGE: The RQ-VAE distance at level l becomes d_{k_{l,c}}(z,e_c) with a per-code curvature magnitude k_{l,c} obtained from the code's standardised quotient curvature; the field is refreshed every 5 epochs from training transitions and enters the assignment logits directly, so both the partition and the codebook gradients move.
SPECIFICATION: {'text': '(1) Build W (24556x24556, symmetrised directed transition counts) from training sequences only. (2) One-off: truncated SVD rank 128 of the row-normalised W gives behaviour coordinates b_i; k-means with exactly K_l clusters gives reference partition P*_l. (3) For any partition a, quotient Q(a) has edge weight w_ab=sum_{i in a,j in b} W_ij; lazy random walk mu_a=0.5 delta_a+0.5 sum_b (w_ab/d_a) delta_b; Ollivier curvature kappa(a,b)=1-W1(mu_a,mu_b)/d_Q(a,b) with d_Q the hop metric; node value kappa_a is the w-weighted mean over neighbours; standardise against S nulls that permute the item-to-cell map while keeping cell sizes: kappa_hat_a=(kappa_a-mean_null)/sd_null. (4) Phi_{l,c}=(kappa_hat_{l,c}-mu*_l)/sd*_l winsorised at +-3 (mu*,sd* from P*_l at the same K_l). (5) k_{l,c}=clip(k0*exp(-Phi_{l,c}), k0/4, 4*k0), k0=min_l ((1-1e-3)/q99(||z_{i,l}||))^2 measured once at init. (6) Assign p(c|i,l) ∝ exp(-d_{k_{l,c}}(z_{i,l},e_{l,c})/tau_l); rest of RQ-VAE unchanged.'}
COST: 72,000 optimizer steps (3000x24), batch 1023. Per-step assignment over 3x256x64 is ~50M mul-adds; the Mobius/artanh path adds ~10 elementwise passes over 0.8M values, under 1 ms/step and under 1% of a model step. Six hundred refreshes (every 5 epochs) cost one 4096-item forward (4 step-equivalents, 2400 step-equivalents total = 3.3%) plus 20 null shuffles x 3 levels x ~5k edges x 4 Sinkhorn iterations, roughly 0.1-1 s each, 1-10 min total. One-off reference SVD+k-means under 15 min. Expected +4-8% wall clock, no extra forward/backward in the 72k steps.
HYPOTHESIS: If per-cell geometry matched to the cell's own quotient curvature is what the generative prefixes need, the produced SID should use more level-3 codes and collide less at fixed K, its standardised curvature profile should move toward the resolution-matched reference profile, and Stage3 test_recall@10 should exceed 0.065 in the single run.
RISKS: ['Per-pair curvature is not a global metric, so cells need not be convex and a code can become over-attractive; node curvature on small cells is noisy and can flip sign between refreshes; if the reference partition is itself strongly aligned with W, Phi may saturate the +-3 clip and the field becomes binary; added curvature could interact badly with the straight-through gradient at level 1 and shrink early code usage, which is exactly the Issue #127 failure mode.']
END IDEA

IDEA: CURVPROF-TRANSPORT-RQ
TITLE: Depth-monotone behaviour-curvature profile that sets the per-level curvature of a hyperbolic residual transport inside the RQ-VAE quantizer
MOTIVATION: The forensic evidence says the recall is not explained by the raw curvature of the behaviour quotient graph but by its standardised profile: level-3 curvature is positively associated with recall (+0.34 over mechanism families), level-1 negatively (-0.16), and the difference L1 minus L3 is negative (-0.20, p=0.0095). Existing SID quantizers cannot act on that, because the partition's curvature is only ever measured after the fact, and because the strongest non-geometric predictor, level-3 code usage (+0.42), collapses when a quantizer is forced toward a coarser behavioural partition (Issue #127: level 1 fell to 4 codes, recall 0.0513). We need a quantizer whose geometry is driven by the measured curvature profile while keeping item-level resolution.
NOVELTY: Earlier arms here changed codebook positions (successor-weighted Frechet), changed radial placement by behaviour entropy, or ran a per-level curvature controller on hard transition scores. This idea does none of those: code positions, codebook size, radii and entropy are untouched. The behaviour curvature sets only the negative curvature c_l of the Poincare ball in which the Möbius log map is taken at the current prefix point, so curvature changes the direction of the residual and therefore which code the next level sees. Removing the behaviour term or replacing the ball by its flat limit changes the code choice at levels 2 and 3, not just a loss value.
CHANGE: For each prefix level, the training-transition quotient graph's standardised Ollivier curvature is turned into a depth-monotone target profile and then into a per-level curvature magnitude c_l; the RQ residual is the curvature-c_l Möbius logarithm of the item point at its accumulated prefix point, so c_l rotates and rescales the residual before nearest-code selection.
SPECIFICATION: {'text': 'Quotient and curvature are computed as below; the quantizer is a hyperbolic RQ-VAE whose only curvature input is c_l from the profile target; per level the assignment is argmin_k ||r_l - e_{l,k}|| with r_l the transported Möbius log at p_{l-1}; the prefix step is a geodesic step of the chosen code. Provenance of every constant: m comes from the measured spread, the sign from the L1<L3 evidence, the clip bounds are two standardised units, the codebook occupancy floor is K/2, the recomputation cadence is a cost budget stated as 61 computations over 3000 epochs.'}
COST: Baseline frozen scale is 24556 training items, 24 steps per epoch, 3000 epochs = 72000 steps. Per step the added work is, for batch 1024 and d=64, two Möbius additions, one artanh, one normalisation and one exp map, about 0.5-1 MFLOP, i.e. roughly +5 to +10 percent of a step; codebook and model size unchanged. Curvature is recomputed 61 times (epoch 1, every 50 epochs, final): each recomputation is one bincount pass over the transition edge list (order 10^6 ints, tens of milliseconds) plus entropic W1 on at most 50000 quotient edges with support capped at 64 neighbours, about 1-3 s. Total curvature overhead about 2-4 minutes, under 5 percent of the 3000-epoch wall clock; memory +O(E) ints and 3 scalars.
HYPOTHESIS: If the signed curvature profile is causal rather than a correlate of code usage, then imposing z_3 > z_1 through the ball curvature should make level-3 cells behaviourally tighter while level 1 stays branchy, and should show up as (a) unchanged or larger level-3 used-code count, (b) z_3 - z_1 > 0 measured on the final SID, (c) Stage3 test recall@10 above 0.065 in the single run.
RISKS: ['The association may be confounded by level-3 code usage, so the mechanism could raise z_3 while recall stays flat; the target could overshoot and saturate distances so that few codes win, which the occupancy guard only catches after the fact; the recomputation lag of 50 epochs may make c_l stale as the partition moves; in the nearly flat regime the transport may be near-identity and the effect may be small; the profile target is derived from a null that is itself noisy at level 3 where many groups are singletons.']
END IDEA
